facts.subject: rule:cgsd-doctoral-enrolment
facts.value: Applicants who are not Canadian citizens, permanent residents or protected persons must be registered in a doctoral programme at an eligible Canadian institution by the application deadline.

readings.value: Applicants who are not Canadian citizens, permanent residents or protected persons must be registered in a doctoral programme at an eligible Canadian institution by the application deadline.
readings.excerpt: If you are not a Canadian citizen, permanent resident of Canada or protected person under subsection 95(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (Canada), you must be registered in your doctoral program of study at an eligible Canadian institution by the application deadline. Up to 15% of awards will be available to international applicants.

facts.subject: rule:cgsd-study-months
facts.value: No more than 36 months of full-time equivalent doctoral study completed by 31 December of the calendar year of application.

readings.value: No more than 36 months of full-time equivalent doctoral study completed by 31 December of the calendar year of application.
readings.excerpt: To be eligible to apply to the CGRS D program, you must have completed no more than 36 months of full-time equivalent study in the doctoral program, the PhD portion of the joint professional undergraduate/PhD program or the joint program for which you are requesting funding by December 31 of the calendar year of your application.

facts.subject: rule:cgsd-other-restrictions
facts.value: Only one CRTAS application per academic year and at most three CGRS D applications are permitted. Previous recipients of a CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC doctoral scholarship, including Vanier, are not eligible.

readings.value: Only one CRTAS application per academic year and at most three CGRS D applications are permitted. Previous recipients of a CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC doctoral scholarship, including Vanier, are not eligible.
readings.excerpt:
You can apply to only one CRTAS program per academic year through CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC. If you apply to more than one program, only the first eligible application submitted to the agencies will be retained.
You can apply a maximum of three times to the CGRS D program.
You cannot have already received a doctoral-level scholarship from CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC (including a Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarship).

facts.subject: rule:cgsd-route-rule
facts.value: Apply through the channel determined by your registration status and the institution’s quota for the chosen agency; the wrong channel causes rejection.

readings.value: Apply through the channel determined by your registration status and the institution’s quota for the chosen agency; the wrong channel causes rejection.
readings.excerpt: You must apply either through a Canadian institution or directly to the appropriate agency, depending on your registration status on the application deadline date and/or your registration status during the calendar year of application. Where you intend to hold the award has no impact on the channel through which you must apply. If you fail to submit your application through the correct channel, your application will be rejected.
